seo_description: Psychological horror game where audio is the core gameplay mechanic. Built with Wwise, Unreal Engine 5, and C++.
hero.title: Shadow Frames
hero.subtitle: Audio Is the Only Weapon
concept.hook: Horror game where sound is the only weapon. No HUD, no markers — just your ears.
concept.p1: Shadow Frames is a psychological horror game set in a 1960s Irish pub rendered entirely in black and white. Anomalies appear every 30 to 50 seconds. Glasses levitate, shadows move on their own, chairs spin. Audio is how you find them.
concept.p2: Sound is not atmosphere, it is the gameplay mechanic. Mute the game and you are blind. Every creak, whisper, and rattle is directional information that guides you to the next anomaly. Photograph it, pin it to the board, piece together the story.
systems.footstep.title: Footstep Detection
systems.footstep.desc: Physics line-trace fires downward from the player's feet each step. The hit result's Physical Material maps to a Wwise Switch: wood, tiles, concrete, creaky wood. New surfaces are added in the editor without touching code.
systems.proximity.title: Enemy Proximity
systems.proximity.desc: A hysteresis state machine with dual thresholds (start at 70%, stop at 60%) prevents audio flickering when the enemy hovers near a boundary. RTPC smoothly scales dread ambience and stress breathing with distance.
systems.anomaly.title: Anomaly System
systems.anomaly.desc: Three-stage detection: alert burst on spawn, directional hint for location, sustained presence loop until captured. RTPC tension scaling drives intensity. Spatial audio cues are the only way to find anomalies. No UI markers.
gallery.title: Wwise Architecture
gallery.desc: Screenshots from the Wwise project showing the mixer hierarchy, DataAsset configurations, RTPC curves, and event structure.
code.title: Technical Deep Dive
code.hint: 3 annotated C++ snippets. Click lines with dots for explanations
challenge1.title: Audio Flickering at Proximity Boundaries
challenge1.hard: When the enemy hovered near the proximity trigger boundary, dread audio toggled on/off every frame. Players heard a machine-gun stutter instead of smooth tension.
challenge1.did: Built a hysteresis state machine with separate start (70%) and stop (60%) thresholds. The 10% gap eliminates boundary flickering. RTPC handles smooth intensity transitions between the thresholds.
challenge2.title: Surface Detection Without Per-Level Setup
challenge2.hard: The pub has 4 floor materials (wood, tiles, concrete, creaky wood). Manually tagging surfaces per level was slow and broke every time the level designer changed geometry.
challenge2.did: Used Unreal's Physical Material system with line traces. Each physics material maps to a Wwise Switch automatically. Designers add new surfaces in the editor — no code changes, no per-level tagging.
